- If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending up, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price momentum is strong.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), model reacts with lag; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment shift is abrupt.  
- Mean reversion is common in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending sideways, model often overfits to recent volatility; use 10-day moving average as baseline.
